sentences.text:
Author: Dipankar Datta Bench: Dipankar Datta  IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA  CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION  CRIMINAL APPEAL No.652/2025  [Arising out of SLP (Crl.) No.12195/2024]
 RATAN KUMAR VERMA & ORS. APPELLANT  VERSUS  THE STATE OF BIHAR & ANR. RESPONDEN  ORDER 1.
Leave granted.

2. The appellants figure as accused in Complaint Case No.1093/2023 under Sections 406 & 420 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 138 of the N.I. Act, pending on the file of the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Patna.
3. In terms of an earlier order dated 02 nd September, 2024, the appellants have deposited Rs.15,00,000/- with the Registry and such amount has been invested in a fixed deposit account.

4. We have noticed from the impugned judgment and order, which denied bail in anticipation of arrest to the appellants, the public prosecutors version that the dispute between the private parties was civil in nature.
5. Prima facie, we are also of the same view.
Accordingly, we set aside the impugned judgment and order.

6. Having regard to the fact of pendency of the complaint before the magistrate, we request such magistrate to decide the proceedings, subject to his convenience, at an early date in accordance with Ratan Kumar Verma vs The State Of Bihar on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194110234/
1 law.
7.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Till such time the complaint is decided, the interim protection granted by this Court protecting the appellants from arrest shall continue but subject to such terms and conditions as may be imposed by the trial court.

The amount of Rs.15,00,000/- deposited by the appellants shall abide by the result of the complaint case or civil suit, if any, instituted by the complainant-respondent,
whichever is earlier.
8.
The deposit of Rs.15,00,000/- shall be treated as payment made in the suitors fund referred to in Chapter XIV of the Supreme Court Rules, 2013.

9. Needless to observe, the appellants shall not, directly or indirectly, by making inducement, threat or promise, dissuade any person acquainted with the facts of the case from disclosing such facts to the court.
10. We clarify that the observations made in this order and grant of bail to the appellants in anticipation of arrest will not be treated as findings on the merits of the case.
11. The appellants shall, however, diligently participate in the ensuing trial and shall not absent themselves without just cause.
12. The appeal is, thus, disposed of in the aforesaid terms.
13. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
